_meta.units: Hartree, total energies, RHF reference, nonrelativistic, C1 (no point-group symmetry)
_meta.geometry: Angstrom geometries from the task. "bohr" runs use the same geometry converted to bohr with PySCF BOHR=0.52917721092 Angstrom (identical nuclear framework to pyscf gto.M(unit="Angstrom")). "angstrom" runs use each program's own conversion factor (MRCC E_nuc off by ~4e-9 rel. to PySCF, CFOUR off by ~2e-6).
_meta.recommended: Compare zccsdt against "recommended" (= bohr-geometry values; MRCC and all three CFOUR CC_PROGs agree to <=2e-12 there).
_meta.basis: Both programs read basis sets from bench/refs/GENBAS (copied as GENBAS into the run dir). cc-pVDZ = GENBAS PVDZ, identical to PySCF cc-pvdz (RHF agrees to 1e-12). 6-31G = GENBAS 6-31G which differs from PySCF built-in 6-31g at ~1e-7 in exponents/coefficients: PySCF built-in RHF is 2.8e-9 (H2O) and 8.9e-8 (N2) below; use bench/refs/genbas2pyscf.py read_genbas() to get the exact GENBAS basis in PySCF (RHF then agrees to <=3e-12).
_meta.convergence: MRCC scftol=12, cctol=11; CFOUR SCF_CONV=11, CC_CONV=11.
_meta.pyscf: PySCF RHF conv_tol=1e-12; PySCF CCSD (conv_tol=1e-11) with GENBAS basis given as a sanity check (agrees to <=5e-10).
_meta.ccsdt(q): CCSDT[Q] and CCSDT(Q) total energies at the bohr geometries: MRCC calc=CCSDT(Q) (inputs MINP.q.bohr) and CFOUR CALC=CCSDT(Q), CC_PROG=NCC (ZMAT.q.bohr); the two programs agree to <= 3e-12 on CCSDT(Q).
_meta.ccsdtq(p): CCSDTQ and CCSDTQ(P) total energies at the bohr geometries: MRCC calc=CCSDTQ(P) (inputs MINP.tqp.bohr; calc=CCSDTQ, MINP.tq.bohr, where there are no pentuples). MRCC prints CCSDTQ[P] and CCSDTQ(P) equal. The *_sto3g systems use the STO-3G of PySCF, written to GENBAS (bench/cfour/genbas.py) and read back for PySCF (zccsdt.genbas.read_genbas), so both programs have the same numbers.
